full_judgment:
3. Plaintiff-Petitioners instituted suit for declaration of title to the land described in the schedule of the plaint. Plaintiff-petitioners filed an application for amendment of plaint and learned Munsif on consideration of the matter allowed the prayer for amendment in respect of inclusion of certain plots into the schedule which were unintentionally left out. But prayer for amendment relating to admission of unregistered barga Kabuliyat was refused. 

 6. In reply to this contention the learned Advocate appearing for the defendant opposite-party submits that the court below exercised its discretion on sound judicial principle and as such the order refusing amendment does not call for any interference. The learned Advocate further submits that on consideration of the facts and circumstances of the case as well as delay being not explained for submitting the unregistered kabuliyat for admission in evidence, the learned Munsif, rightly refused the prayer for amendment. It is further submitted the unregistered kabuliyat sought to be admitted into evidence under the garb of amendment but in fact it is an attempt to admit the unregistered document into evidence at a last stage and this matter will be governed by Order 7 rule 18 of the Code of Civil Procedure and that delay for producing unregistered kabuliyat being not explained, the Trial Court was justified in refusing to admit that document into evidence. In support of this contention the learned Advocate for the defendant opposite Party relied on a decision in the case of Ronda and ors. Vs. Waghu reported in 3 DLR 311. It is a decision of the Privy Council. 

 11. In the instant case unregistered kabuliyat was sought to be given in evidence 10 years after the plaint was presented in Court. The suit was filed in the year 1976 and the amendment petition was filed on 19.9.85 i.e. 10 years after presentation of the plaint in Court. But the inordinate delay remains unexplained. Further the amendment petition involved setting up of a new case necessitating framing of new issue. In the cited case appellant applied for leave from the court of the Subordinate Judge for admission into evidence the certified copy of the two extracts from public document. This leave was sought after the evidence was closed and suit was adjourned for argument. The learned Subordinate Judge refused the leave and being aggrieved by that order, the matter was taken upto Privy Council and their Lordships of the Privy Council held that the Subordinate Judge exercised his discretion on sound judicial principle in refusing to admit the document at the late stage. 

 12. In the instant case, the application for amendment does not disclose reason why 10 years delay occurred in filing amendment petition seeking admission of unregistered kabuliyat. Further, it appears that the land involved in the suit does not appear to be identical with the land mentioned in unregistered kabuliyat and this will necessitate framing of new issue. Be that as it may, since the unregistered kabuliyat was not filed along with the plaint though it was in possession of the plaintiff opposite party and the delay in making application for admission of that document having not been explained, the learned court below exercised his jurisdiction properly in refusing the amendment. In view of this fact the impugned order does not call for any interference.
